   For the 11 million 401(k) plan participants that hold nearly half a trillion dollars in Capital Group’s target-date funds, the withdrawal approaches are intended to be an informational starting point for figuring out an often stressful problem: how much to withdraw from a nest egg, without running the risk of depleting it too quickly.

   Financial products offered by Chinese financial institutions are growing faster than retail deposits, Moody’s Ratings says in a commentary. It estimates that outstanding balances of these products rose 15.5% in 2025, accelerating from 13.9% in 2024, citing data from asset managers and Chinese regulators. Retail deposit growth in the nation slowed to 9.7% from 10.4% over the same period. “Most of the underlying investments are liquid standard assets, such as bonds and money market funds, rather than illiquid nonstandard credit assets,” it says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

   Investors aren’t simply disappearing from the housing market, Realtor.com says. Their presence is changing. In the first half of 2026, smaller investors strengthened their hold while large and mega investors pulled back. Cash remains a defining feature of investor purchases, yet the investor and overall market all-cash share fell in the first half of 2026 as climbing inventory and softer market conditions eased all-cash buying. Investors accounted for 10.7% of home purchases. However, the number of homes they bought fell to its lowest first-half level since 2020. Investor selling eased slightly as well, but its share of home sales remained above pandemic- and pre-pandemic-era levels. Together, the trends point to a cooler market, not a uniform retreat by every kind of investor. (chris.wack@wsj.com@wsj.com)

VERNON YUEN/ZUMA PRESS
 

One of the biggest retirement-fund managers in the U.S. is weighing in on the hot-button issue of how to draw down your 401(k) nest egg.

 

Capital Group, the country’s largest manager of active target-date funds, will start offering research-backed withdrawal strategies for holders of its funds. The investment manager landed on two different approaches, depending on a person’s goals and expenses, after studying the hypothetical performance of a retirement portfolio across market scenarios. It is set to publish recommended annual withdrawal ranges and the research supporting them on Wednesday.

 

For the 11 million 401(k) plan participants that hold nearly half a trillion dollars in Capital Group’s target-date funds, the withdrawal approaches are intended to be an informational starting point for figuring out an often stressful problem: how much to withdraw from a nest egg, without running the risk of depleting it too quickly.

 

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

 
 
 

Planning & Investing

 

Healthcare Stocks Are Rallying, and Flashing a Warning for the Rest of the Market

 

Healthcare stocks no longer trade at a discount to the broader market. That isn’t a reason to sell.

 
 
 

Market Talk

 

From Dow Jones Newswires

 

Financial products offered by Chinese financial institutions are growing faster than retail deposits, Moody’s Ratings says in a commentary. It estimates that outstanding balances of these products rose 15.5% in 2025, accelerating from 13.9% in 2024, citing data from asset managers and Chinese regulators. Retail deposit growth in the nation slowed to 9.7% from 10.4% over the same period. “Most of the underlying investments are liquid standard assets, such as bonds and money market funds, rather than illiquid nonstandard credit assets,” it says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

 

Investors aren’t simply disappearing from the housing market, Realtor.com says. Their presence is changing. In the first half of 2026, smaller investors strengthened their hold while large and mega investors pulled back. Cash remains a defining feature of investor purchases, yet the investor and overall market all-cash share fell in the first half of 2026 as climbing inventory and softer market conditions eased all-cash buying. Investors accounted for 10.7% of home purchases. However, the number of homes they bought fell to its lowest first-half level since 2020. Investor selling eased slightly as well, but its share of home sales remained above pandemic- and pre-pandemic-era levels. Together, the trends point to a cooler market, not a uniform retreat by every kind of investor. (chris.wack@wsj.com@wsj.com)
